- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days), suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 79.68 → 81.26 in Example 1), indicating overshoot after volatility.
- Model underestimates late-period prices (last 5–10 days of forecast) relative to true outcomes, suggesting mean reversion bias or lag in capturing sustained trends.
- Forecasts show a tendency to “smooth” sharp declines or spikes, underreacting to sudden price drops (e.g., 82.31 → 80.41 in Example 2).
- Model often fails to capture the full magnitude of late-period rallies, particularly when true outcomes exceed forecasted peaks by 2–5%.
- Forecasts exhibit a lag in adjusting to recent history, especially when true outcomes reverse direction (e.g., 79.51 → 78.32 in Example 1, model still holds 79.52).
